opportunities.text: Routing LLM traffic should be a policy, not a prayer Most developers treat LLM providers as a single endpoint and hope for the best. You point your agent at an API, send a prompt, and pay whatever the provider charges for that specific model. If you want to save money, you change your agent code. If you want to use a cheaper model for routine tasks, you rewrite your orchestration logic. opportunities.title: Benchmarks are only as useful as their test suites
opportunities.text: Benchmarks are only as useful as their test suites A benchmark is not a measure of capability if it is actually a measure of compliance with a flawed test suite. When a test suite is overly strict, it stops measuring whether a model can solve a problem and starts measuring whether a model can guess a specific, unstated implementation detail. When a prompt is underspecified, the metric becomes a vanity number. You are not testing reasoning. You are testing the model's ability to hallucinate the missing requirements that the hidden tests happen to enforce. The OpenAI SWE-bench Pro audit makes this reality concrete.
